_comment: How a room renders: fog, beam brightness, surface reflectance.
Every one of these was eyeballed against a SINGLE PHOTOGRAPH of one
room. That is honest for despacio and means nothing for anywhere else,
which is why they are a named profile a venue can replace rather than
constants a second room would have to be talked out of.
Merged per KEY over the built-in defaults in previz/config.py, so a room
that only needs different fog says only that -- a venue block restating
all seven would drift the first time one of them was improved.
The re-sweep procedure, which ray_gain's own comment has always asked
for whenever the room size or the beam angle changes:
1. Build the level and park a look with one head lit --
python previz/ball_check.py --artnet 127.0.0.1 --seconds 300
2. Snapshot the 'overview' and 'audience' views.
3. beam_gain until the shaft reads as bright as the dot it lands on,
then dot_gain until the landing spot is not a blown white disc.
4. beam_extinction_per_m until a beam crossing the whole room fades
about as much as it does in the room.
5. ray_gain last: it is the one that changes most with room size,
because the shafts are drawn over a distance the room decides.
6. Re-snapshot both views and compare against a photo of the real
room at the same look. If there is no photo, say so in the venue
block rather than implying these were measured.

despacio room._comment: The originals. Tuned 2026-08 against one photo of an 18 m room with 8-degree beams and a 9 m truss frame.
